newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's first U.S. Hard Rock Cafe outlet opens.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's first U.S. Hard Rock Cafe outlet opens.

text.p: The hamburger and rock-and-roll restaurant chain Hard Rock Cafe opened for business in the Jordanian capital of Amman on Friday, only the second of its kind in the Arab world so far, as the U.S. group expands its presence in the region, businessmen said.

Jordanian and Saudi investors won the 20-year franchise for $1 million from Beirut-based Hard Rock Cafe Middle East Inc (HRCME), which had secured the exclusive rights from the U.S. firm to all the Middle East and North Africa region including Turkey except Israel, businessmen said.
The Saudi Arabian Jeddah based Bin-Laden Group, which owns the Beirut based HRCME, is also major shareholder in the Amman outlet.
The project, which cost over three million dollars, covers a 2,200 square metre area of bars, merchandise shops and a function room with a total seating for 250 people.
Amman's Hard Rock Cafe ranks in the top five league in terms of size among the Orlando-based U.S. chain's 81 worldwide outlets, the owners said.

The owners said the restaurant, by far the most extravagent food chain outlet so far to be set up in the kingdom, caters for a growing Westernised Jordanian middle class and will boost the country's expanding tourism industry.
The Amman outlet, the second to open in the Arab world after Lebanon's Hard Rock Cafe, will be followed by the opening of a similar venture in Bahrain next September.
The Saudi investors plan along with local partners other Hard Rock Cafe outlets in major Middle Eastern cities, including Dubai, Ankara, Cairo, and the Sharm al Sheikh resort in Egypt.
